problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(0,12).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{12}^{2}} \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies on the positive half of $y$-axis, we have $\theta =\frac{\pi }{2}.$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(12,\frac{\pi }{2}).$
